paragraphs.source_en: North of the main hall of Shōhō-ji Temple in Inukami District, Ōmi, stood Sawayama Castle. The temple's ginkgo leaves had begun to turn yellow. That day, two uninvited visitors on magnificent horses arrived at the temple: Ishida Mitsunari and his chief retainer, Shima Sakon Katsutake. The two sent away both the abbot who came to greet them and the young monk who hurried forward with tea, then devoted themselves to admiring the autumn colors.

paragraphs.source_en: “You needn't trouble yourselves. The weather is fine today, and we were out for a long ride. We happened to pass your temple and wished only to rest awhile.” With that, Mitsunari dismissed the abbot.
